newsitem.title: USA: Metal Recovery to provide dezincing plant plans.
newsitem.headline: Metal Recovery to provide dezincing plant plans.

text.p: Metal Recovery Technologies Inc said it will provide proposals to two United States steel manufacturers and one foundry operator for building and operating dezincing plants at or near their facilities.
Metal Recovery also expects to respond with a proposal within 60 days to a February 25, 1997 request for a plan for a dezincing facility for General Motors Corp, a company spokesman said.

"Combined with the GM plant currently beging proposed, these plants will have the potential to recycle in excess of $200 million worth of steel scrap and zinc per year," said Michael Lucas, chairman of Metal Recovery, in a statement.

Metal Recovery uses a patent-pending process that removes zinc from galvanized steel scrap producing 99.8 percent pure zinc and a high qualilty reusable scrap steel. The technology has been developed by Metal Recovery and the Argonne National Laboratory and the United States Department of Energy.
